fix: Add a non-allocating `pub(crate) fn first_id(&self) -> Option<WindowId>` to the window registry next to `ids()` (crates/incular-runtime/src/window_state.rs:303) that scans the slots the same way `ids()` does and returns the first live id. Then replace the fallback with `self.registry.borrow().first_id()`. This removes the Vec allocation per work item when the primary window has closed.

Drop the per-window intermediate Vec. Use `.flat_map(|window| registry.get(window).map(|record| { let root = record.runtime.devtools_reactive_root(); let tree = record.runtime.tree(); entries.iter().filter(move |(entry_root, _)| *entry_root == root).filter_map(move |(_, element)| tree.devtools_id_for_element(*element).map(|dev_id| incular_devtools_protocol::SignalSubscriber { signal, element: dev_id, path: tree.devtools_element_path(*element) })) }))` so the Option of the iterator is flattened directly and the `let Some(record) ... else { return Vec::new(); }` branch disappears.
